To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal number of processors on a chip increases as the number of memory channels increases, as the memory bandwidth increases, as the processor clock frequency decreases, as the memory clock frequency increases, as the communication latency decreases, and as the processor power increases.

the optimal number of cores for a given application and architecture depends on the ratio of the energy-delay cost of the communication network to the energy-delay cost in the processor and that the number of cores is inversely proportional to the number of threads.

(a) the optimal CMP architecture is a function of the application mix, (b) the number of cores is the dominant factor in determining the optimal CMP architecture, and (c) the optimal CMP design is a function of both the application mix and the area constraint of the single die.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of designing and optimizing computer systems for energy-delay efficiency.
the design of computer systems that are both high performance and low power.
the development of a quantitative and general methodology for evaluating parallel computer architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the objective function is useful for the design and analysis of computer systems.

the objective function is a powerful and flexible tool that can be used to evaluate the impact of architectural parameters on system performance and energy consumption, and can be used as a guide to optimize the design of computer systems under different constraints.

the objective function presented here offers an analytical framework to explore the design space of parallel computer architectures, and is an important step towards the design of energy efficient parallel architectures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have derived a general objective function for computer architectures that links the gains in parallel processing to the cost in energy and delay.
we present an analytical framework that links the performance gains in a multiprocessor system to the microarchitecture and system design choices.
we have developed a general analytical framework that can be used to optimize system performance, energy, and delay for any architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single, objective, analytical function can capture the performance, energy and delay characteristics of a multiprocessor architecture.
a general analytical formulation of system performance in terms energy and delay can provide the foundation for the rapid evaluation of microarchitectural and architectural design alternatives.
the objective function can be used for a variety of architectural optimization problems, and that it provides a quantitative measure of system cost that can be compared to the cost of other systems.
